title: The Seeker Who Crossed Three Lands
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Salman al-Farisi's journey toward faith spanned so many years and so much distance that it reads almost like an extended pilgrimage rather than a single conversion.
Narrator: [reflective] Born in Persia into a household devoted to fire-worship, he grew disillusioned early, sensing that something essential remained missing from those rigid rituals.
Narrator: [serious] After encountering a Christian congregation whose devotion struck him as more genuine, he abandoned his family entirely, choosing exile over spiritual stagnation.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He studied under several successive monks across different regions, each one, before dying, directing him toward yet another teacher rumored to hold deeper understanding.
Narrator: [with feeling] The final monk told him a prophet was soon expected in Arabia, one who would bear specific signs, including a distinctive mark between his shoulders.
Narrator: [tense] Determined to find this figure, Salman joined a caravan heading south, only to be betrayed and sold into slavery along the way.
Narrator: [calm] For years, he served various owners in Arabia, quietly enduring servitude while never abandoning the hope that had propelled his entire journey.
Narrator: [with wonder] When he eventually heard of the Prophet's arrival nearby, he tested the claims cautiously, offering charity first, since prophets reportedly wouldn't personally consume it.
Narrator: [warmly] Every detail matched what the dying monks had described, and upon seeing the mark himself, Salman finally embraced what he'd spent decades pursuing.
Narrator: [serious] His most celebrated contribution came later, during a siege, when he proposed digging a defensive trench, a tactic unfamiliar to Arabian warfare at the time.
Narrator: [reflective] The strategy, borrowed from Persian military tradition, ultimately stalled the attacking forces long enough to save the entire besieged community.
Narrator: [with admiration] The Prophet reportedly declared that Salman belonged to his own household, dissolving whatever tribal boundaries might otherwise have defined his belonging.
Narrator: [thoughtful] What moves me isn't merely his eventual arrival at faith, but his willingness to keep searching, decade after decade, without any guarantee of finding it.
Narrator: [warmly] Salman's story reminds me that sincere seeking, however prolonged or circuitous, rarely goes entirely unanswered in the end.
